Adorn

/uh-DORN/ - rhymes with corn · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Adorn means to decorate.

Jewelers in the old quarter adorn even their doorframes with hammered tin stars.

Worked Example

For the ambassador's farewell dinner, the embassy staff adorned the ballroom with silk swags and white orchids, and the plain government hall suddenly looked like a palace.

Adorn is warmer and more deliberate than just 'put things on': it means adding touches whose whole purpose is beauty. The staff didn't repair or rearrange the ballroom — they dressed it up, which is exactly the work adorn names.

How Adorn Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

garnish

garnish: adds finishing touches, almost always to plates of food

bedeck

bedeck: drapes something in finery, often to excess

Antonyms

strip

strip: removes every decoration or covering

disfigure

disfigure: ruins a look instead of improving it

How Strong Is It? — trim → adorn → festoon

trim vs. adorn

trim vs. adorn: To trim is the lightest touch of decoration — a ribbon at a cuff — stopping well short of adorn.

festoon vs. adorn

festoon vs. adorn: To festoon goes further than adorn: garlands looped from every beam until the ceiling itself disappears.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-

Prefix — ad-: to, onto

Root — orn-

Root — orn-: to decorate, to equip (Latin ornare)

Put it together

Put it together: Ad- (onto) + orn- (to decorate) = to put decoration onto something. Latin ornare gave English a small family of dressing-up words, and adorn is its verb of action: you take a plain surface and fasten beauty to it.

Use the root in a new word: ornate

Use the root in a new word: ornate: The theater's ornate lobby drips with carved cherubs and gold moldings.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, slightly formal

Adorn is a shade more elegant than the everyday 'decorate' — reach for it when the touches are graceful and deliberate. If the decoration hangs in loops and chains, festoon is more exact, and when you're describing the finished, heavily decorated result rather than the act, this unit's ornate is the word.
